ep01.h.d1_office.l03: Four statements. Four apartments with strangers living in them. And not one body.
ep01.h.d1_office.doc_doc_statement:
To the Prosecutor of Kuntsevo District, Moscow, from Galina Vasilyevna Somova, Molodogvardeyskaya St., apt. 33.

STATEMENT

I request that my neighbor, Zoya Pavlovna of apt. 34, be located. No one has seen her since the end of June. Strangers are living in her apartment and say they bought it. Zoya Pavlovna had no plans to go anywhere—she would have told me.

August 2, 1993. Somova
ep01.h.d1_office.l04: Gromov? Viktor Saiko, MUR—Moscow criminal police. I brought you these. Molodogvardeyskaya is first. The other three: Fili, Presnya, Kuntsevo again.
ep01.h.d1_office.l06: An old person lives alone. The old person vanishes. A month later, new people—and paperwork you could frame.
ep01.h.d1_office.l07: I checked Molodogvardeyskaya: the buyers are the Lapins, the sale was notarized on Presnya by Kovrigin. The rest is your job.
ep01.h.d1_call.l01: Palych, the head of the unit. He calls when he’s unhappy—which means always.
ep01.h.d1_call.l02: Gromov, the pensioners. A preliminary inquiry, not a case. By Friday: a flaw in the paperwork, you open a case. No flaw, a refusal to open one. And don’t make a fuss.
ep01.h.d1_call.l04: Five days until Friday. To find people nobody is looking for.
ep01.h.d1_go.l01: So, Counselor? The car’s downstairs, half a tank of gas.
ep01.h.d1_go.c_d1_go.flat: To Molodogvardeyskaya. Let’s see the apartment
ep01.h.d1_go.c_d1_go.galina: To the neighbor who wrote the statement
ep01.h.d1_go.c_d1_go.notary: To Presnya, to see the notary Kovrigin
ep01.h.route_car.l01: “Citizen”… I wouldn’t open the door either. Old ladies like the patronymic.
ep01.h.route_car.l02: A gray Volga under her windows. Maybe twenty thousand in Moscow. Not a million anymore.
ep01.h.route_car.l03: You told them straight that they could lose the apartment. Now they’ll either help us or run to a lawyer.
ep01.h.route_car.l04: They’ve got a kid. Shame. You got the papers, though—that counts.
ep01.h.route_car.l05: We came in empty-handed and left empty-handed. Now he’ll be on the phone.
ep01.h.route_car.l06: The typewriter girl never took her eyes off you. She has something to say—just not in front of the boss.
ep01.h.route_car.l07: That girl is scared to death. Sergei Viktorovich is practically one of their own.
ep01.h.route_car.l08: Kovrigin sweated like in a sauna. Not from the heat.
ep01.h.route_car.l09: He even brought her chocolate… Polite. The bastard.
ep01.h.route_car.l12: Not a coincidence anymore. An assembly line.
ep01.h.route_car.l13: We’ve got a name. Murashov, S. V., by power of attorney.
ep01.h.route_car.c_route_d1.flat: To Molodogvardeyskaya Street, to see the Lapins
ep01.h.route_car.c_route_d2_1.flat: To Molodogvardeyskaya Street, to see the Lapins

ep01.h.go_flat.l01: Apartment thirty-four. The Lapins live there now. I’ll see what papers they bought it on—and what the owner left behind.
ep01.h.go_flat.l02: Galina said Zoya Pavlovna had no plans to go anywhere. We’ll check.
ep01.h.go_galina.l01: Galina Vasilyevna wrote the statement. She lives across the landing—she must know who visited Zoya Pavlovna.
ep01.h.go_galina.l02: And whether she ever saw the man who sold the apartment—Murashov.
ep01.h.go_notary.l01: Kovrigin notarized the power of attorney dated June fourteenth. With the papers in hand, I’ll ask who brought Zoya Pavlovna to him.
ep01.h.go_notary.l02: Kovrigin notarized the sale. Without papers he’ll stall—but he’s worth a look.
ep01.h.go_notary.l03: And I’ll ask how she read the document without glasses.
ep01.h.go_zhek.l01: Housing office passport desk: Zoya Pavlovna was taken off the residence register. Who applied—and was he seen there before?
ep01.h.go_bti.l01: The BTI, the technical inventory bureau, records every apartment deal. If Murashov has done this before, it’s in the card file.
ep01.h.go_bti.l02: The BTI, the technical inventory bureau, records every apartment deal. If the man with the power of attorney has done this before, it’s on file.
ep01.h.flat.l02: Wallpaper stripped to the newspapers. The china cabinet stands where it stood, amid a stranger’s remodel.
ep01.h.flat.l03: We didn’t break any rules. Bought it by contract, at a notary’s. Paid every last kopeck.
ep01.h.flat.l04: They told us the old lady went to relatives down south. She left the cabinet—said she didn’t need it.
ep01.h.flat.c_flat.prompt: What to say to the Lapins?
ep01.h.flat.c_flat.formal: Show me the contract. If it’s legal, there’s nothing to fear
ep01.h.flat.c_flat.truth: The sale could be declared invalid. Help us
ep01.h.flat_formal.l01: Here. A copy of the contract and of the power of attorney. The notary said it’s all clean.

ep01.h.flat_truth.l01: What do you mean, invalid? We saved for ten years. We have a child.
ep01.h.flat_truth.l02: Here. The contract, the power of attorney. The middleman rushed us: cash, right at the notary’s, in the hallway. Said it’d be faster.

ep01.h.flat_look.l01: Counselor. Check the cabinet. Behind the glass.
ep01.h.flat_look.c_flat_photo.later: Don’t touch without attesting witnesses. Back with Levina
ep01.h.flat_inspect.l01: The owner “went south.” Let’s see what she took with her—and what she left behind.
ep01.h.flat_inspect_fail.l01: Will you be long? Our child is asleep.
ep01.h.flat_inspect_done.l01: Relatives in the south, you say? She has one grandson. In Samara.
ep01.h.flat_inspect_done.l02: That’s what we were told… We didn’t know.
ep01.h.flat_inspect_done.l03: Can’t dig further with the owners watching. Levina will do it by the book, with attesting witnesses.

ep01.h.galina.l02: Apartments 33 and 34 face each other across the landing. Zoya Pavlovna’s door is new now, steel. Galina’s opens on the chain.
ep01.h.galina.l03: The police again? I wrote it all. Everything I knew.
ep01.h.galina.c_galina.formal: Citizen Somova, your testimony needs an official record
ep01.h.galina.c_galina.human: Galina Vasilyevna, off the record. Who came to see her?
ep01.h.galina_closed.l01: An official record… I saw nothing. End of June she left with a bag, that’s all. Write what you like.
ep01.h.galina_closed.c_landing_g1.flat: Go see the Lapins, in apartment thirty-four
ep01.h.galina_closed.c_landing_g1.notary: Drive to Presnya, to the notary
ep01.h.galina_open.l01: The chain drops. Galina steps onto the threshold in slippers and whispers, as if someone behind the steel door were listening.
ep01.h.galina_open.l02: One man visited her… Sergei. Three weeks or so, helping with her papers. Polite. Said he was from a newspaper.
ep01.h.galina_open.l03: Did he give a last name?
ep01.h.galina_open.l04: No. She called him by name and patronymic—Sergei Viktorovich. He came in a Volga, a gray one. Parked under my windows, not by the entrance.
ep01.h.galina_open.l05: The last time she went out was the end of June. With a bag, in her good raincoat. Said Sergei Viktorovich would stop by about the papers. Never saw her again.
ep01.h.galina_open.l06: And what if he finds out it was me?
ep01.h.galina_open.c_galina_fear.promise: Your name won’t come up anywhere
ep01.h.galina_open.c_galina_fear.duty: If needed, we’ll call you to court. It’s your duty
ep01.h.galina_end.l01: Well, don’t let me down. I trusted you.
ep01.h.galina_end.l02: Duty… I’ve done my share. My daughter’s in Tula—I’ll go to her while you catch him.
ep01.h.galina_end.c_landing_g2.flat: Go see the Lapins, in apartment thirty-four
ep01.h.galina_end.c_landing_g2.notary: Drive to Presnya, to the notary
ep01.h.notary.l02: A line out to the doors. Kovrigin sees us right away—and he clearly doesn’t like it.
ep01.h.notary.l03: Prosecutor’s office? Come in. But quickly—people have waited since morning, and I have one assistant.
ep01.h.notary_bare.l01: We’re interested in the Molodogvardeyskaya transaction. June.
ep01.h.notary_bare.l02: Young man, I handle hundreds of those. A registry number, a date—or an official request. Through the city prosecutor’s office.
ep01.h.notary_bare.c_notary_bare.insist: You’re required to show the registry to an investigator
ep01.h.notary_bare.c_notary_bare.retreat: Fine. We’ll come back with a request
ep01.h.notary_insist.l01: Required, yes. On request. Good day, Comrade Investigator.
ep01.h.notary_retreat.l01: Now that’s right. Procedure is procedure.
ep01.h.notary_retreat.l02: The girl at the typewriter hasn’t typed one letter this whole time.
ep01.h.notary_papers.l01: Power of attorney, June fourteenth. Zoya Pavlovna. The attorney-in-fact—Murashov.
ep01.h.notary_papers.l02: Yes, yes, I remember. An elderly woman, everything read aloud, everything signed. Within my competence, it was all lawful.
ep01.h.notary_papers.c_notary_ask.regist: Show me the registry entry for June fourteenth
ep01.h.notary_papers.c_notary_ask.glasse: How did she read the power of attorney without glasses?
ep01.h.notary_glasses.l01: Glasses?… She had none. The attorney-in-fact read the text aloud, in my presence. The law permits it.
ep01.h.notary_glasses.l02: So Murashov himself read the power of attorney to her. What he actually read, only he knows.
ep01.h.notary_glasses.l03: A pen fell behind the typewriter. The assistant bent down for it and isn’t hurrying to get up.
ep01.h.notary_reg.l01: Here you are. The principal’s signature, the fee paid.
ep01.h.notary_reg_ins.l01: The entry is there. Only the ink is bluer than in the neighboring lines—as if it was added later.
ep01.h.notary_reg2.l01: A clerical slip by my assistant. It happens.
ep01.h.notary_reg2.l02: A pen fell behind the typewriter. The assistant bent down for it and isn’t hurrying to get up.
ep01.h.notary_who.l01: He brought her in—Sergei Viktorovich Murashov. Decent man, polite, explained everything to the old lady himself.

ep01.h.notary_alone.l04: Prosecutor’s office? Come in. But quickly—my assistant is on vacation, I’m alone with this whole line.

ep01.h.notary_lyuda_q.l01: Counselor, the girl’s about to cry. I’ll step out on the stairs for a smoke. She’ll follow, you’ll see.
ep01.h.notary_lyuda_q.c_lyuda.prompt: Saiko offers to talk to the assistant
ep01.h.lyuda.l02: I don’t know anything. I’ve worked here six months.
ep01.h.lyuda.l03: It’s not about you. It’s about Sergei Viktorovich. Does he come often?
ep01.h.lyuda.l04: Often. Always with old people, always without waiting in line. He pays cash for the rush—straight into Anatoly Nikolaevich’s desk.
ep01.h.lyuda.l05: Just don’t tell him I said so. He already yells that I see too much.
ep01.h.zhek.l02: A line, a little window, the smell of a wet rag. Every privatization starts here: certificates, extracts, stamps.
ep01.h.zhek.l03: Thirty-four? Taken off the register June twenty-fifth. On application.
ep01.h.zhek.l05: Not herself. The man with the power of attorney—he had the paper. Polite sort, brought me a chocolate bar. Said the old lady was going to relatives.
ep01.h.zhek.l06: What else? Make it quick—I have people waiting.
ep01.h.zhek.c_zhek.prompt: One question, and make it quick
ep01.h.zhek.c_zhek.name: What’s his last name? It should be on the application
ep01.h.zhek.c_zhek.name_check: Is it Murashov? Check the application
ep01.h.zhek_name.l01: On the application… Murashov. Sergei Viktorovich. Notarized power of attorney, everything in order.
ep01.h.zhek_seen.l01: Oh, he’s been hanging around our line all summer. Talking to the old ladies, filling out forms for them. I thought he was somebody’s son.
ep01.h.bti.cap01: BTI archive. Open Tuesdays and Thursdays
ep01.h.bti.l02: Saiko stayed in the car: papers are my department. Raisa Lvovna looks at my ID longer than she looks at me.
ep01.h.bti.l03: No visitors on Wednesdays. Well, since you’re here…
ep01.h.bti.l04: The prosecutor’s office… A request? Without one, only by address.
ep01.h.bti.l06: Title transfer—agreement dated June twenty-eighth. Notary Kovrigin. The seller’s representative under a power of attorney—Murashov, S. V.
ep01.h.bti.l07: And other transactions—same notary, same representative?
ep01.h.bti.l08: That I can’t do without a request, dear.
ep01.h.bti.c_bti.plead: Raisa Lvovna, old people are vanishing. Four already
ep01.h.bti_chain.l01: …Four, you say? Kovrigin and this Murashov? Look yourself. One hour till lunch.
ep01.h.bti_chain_ok.l01: Six cards. Six apartments in a summer. The notary is always Kovrigin, the man with the power of attorney always Murashov.
ep01.h.bti_chain_ok.l02: Six… My God. All of them living alone.
ep01.h.bti_chain_part.l01: Three cards, and then Raisa Lvovna shut the drawer: lunch. Notary Kovrigin, attorney-in-fact Murashov. And that’s not all.
ep01.h.bti_chain_fail.l01: Lunch. Come Thursday, with a written request.
ep01.h.bti_chain_fail.l02: A whole hour in the card file, and not one card except ours.
ep01.h.bti_formal.l01: Then come Thursday, dear. We don’t see visitors on Wednesdays.
ep01.h.bti_formal.l02: Thursday. That leaves one day until Friday.
ep01.h.bti_formal.l03: Then come tomorrow, dear. With a written request.
ep01.h.bti_formal.l04: Tomorrow I won’t have time for card files.
ep01.h.d1_evening.l02: By evening the office empties out. A lamp, a typewriter under its cover, and Levina with three glasses of tea.
ep01.h.d1_evening.l03: Tea’s hot, the cigarette’s mine. Tell me what you dug up.
ep01.h.d1_evening.l04: Give me the power of attorney and contract. Side by side.
ep01.h.d1_lens.l01: Power of attorney and contract, side by side under the lamp. They don’t match somewhere. Look.
ep01.h.d1_lens_ok.l01: The contract says the power of attorney is dated June eleventh, but the power of attorney itself is dated the fourteenth. Under the lamp: a four over a one. And no “correction certified” note.
ep01.h.d1_lens_fail.l01: I don’t see it, Gromov. My eyes glaze over by evening. An ordinary document.
ep01.h.d1_eve_rest.l01: There’s your flawed document, Gromov. Open the case. Palych will grumble and sign.
ep01.h.d1_eve_rest.l02: We have the papers, but no flaw in them. Palych will call it a refusal. Four days until Friday.
ep01.h.d1_eve_rest.l03: “Sergei” and a gray Volga are something. But no flawed document, and four days until Friday.
ep01.h.d1_eve_rest.l04: An empty day is still a day. There are only four left until Friday.
ep01.h.d1_eve_rest.l05: The china cabinet, huh? I’ll go tomorrow with attesting witnesses. Once it’s in a report, it’s in the file.
ep01.h.d1_eve_rest.l06: Her glasses are at home, and her signature is steady. So somebody else read it to her.
ep01.h.d1_eve_rest.l07: She left her nitroglycerin? You don’t go south without that, Gromov.
ep01.h.d1_eve_rest.x_calendar: The calendar stops at June twenty-seventh, and by the twenty-eighth they were selling her apartment. Nobody’s seen her since.
ep01.h.d1_eve_rest.x_pension: And her pension certificate is on the bed. She meant to be gone briefly, and never came back.
ep01.h.d1_eve_rest.l08: A guy I know on Presnya called. Kovrigin sent his assistant on vacation today, starting tomorrow. She didn’t leave an address.
ep01.h.d1_eve_rest.l09: The Lapins called someone the minute we left. Or the notary figured it all out himself.
ep01.h.d1_eve_call.l01: Gromov! The city prosecutor’s office called. Notary Kovrigin says an investigator keeps barging in without a request. What do you think you’re doing?
ep01.h.d1_eve_call.l03: Yeah, Mom. I’ll be late. Soup’s on the stove, I’ll heat it.
ep01.h.d1_eve_call.l04: Somewhere in Moscow a gray Volga is on the road. Its owner has plans for tomorrow, too.
ep01.h.d1_eve_call.l05: Somewhere in Moscow walks the man who sold Zoya Pavlovna’s apartment. He has plans for tomorrow, too.
ep01.h.d2_office.l02: Palych came in person. That’s worse than a call.
ep01.h.d2_office.l03: Opened the case? Watch yourself. It’s yours now, and I’ll hold you responsible, not MUR.
ep01.h.d2_office.l04: Don’t bother the notary unless you must. Notarial Chamber member.
ep01.h.d2_office.l05: The notary’s a Notarial Chamber member. The city prosecutor’s office called. Friday, Gromov, and quietly.
ep01.h.d2_office.l06: Friday, remember? A flawed document, or it’s a refusal.
ep01.h.d2_office.c_boss.push: Four people are already missing, Valentin Pavlovich
ep01.h.d2_push.l01: Four, five… You’ve got papers, not bodies. Get to work.
ep01.h.d2_calls.l01: Gromov, I’m at Molodogvardeyskaya. Photo seized, attesting witnesses signed. On the back: “To Grandma from her grandson. Samara.”
ep01.h.d2_calls.l02: And her glasses, on the china cabinet, on their case. And the nitroglycerin from the windowsill. All in the report.
ep01.h.d2_calls.l03: And her glasses, on the china cabinet, on their case. Also in the report.
ep01.h.d2_calls.l04: And the nitroglycerin from the windowsill. Also in the report.
ep01.h.d2_calls.x_seized_cal: The calendar off the wall—the page says June twenty-seventh. Also in the report.
ep01.h.d2_calls.x_seized_pen: And the pension ID from the bed.
ep01.h.d2_calls.l05: This is Irina Lapina. After you left yesterday, my husband called the notary. The middleman told us: if anyone comes, call.
ep01.h.d2_calls.l06: So the notary and the middleman are in this together.
ep01.h.d2_go.l01: Well, Counselor, shall we? I filled the tank.

ep01.h.d2_night.l02: The office is empty. A lamp, files, Saiko and Levina by the open window.
ep01.h.d2_night.l03: Stopped by Galina’s to get the report signed. Neighbors say she’s gone to Tula, to her daughter. You’ve got no witness now.
ep01.h.d2_night.l04: Lay it out. How do you think it went? Go by the papers, not feelings.

ep01.h.d_how.d_how.notary: A deal like this wouldn’t pass without a notary
ep01.h.d_how_w1.l01: No weak spot? Go to sleep. I’ll wait till you find one.
ep01.h.d_where.d_where.left: She left with him in late June and vanished
ep01.h.d_where.d_where.vypiska: Deregistered in her absence. They knew she wouldn’t be back
ep01.h.d_where.d_where.unknown: I don’t know. But no one has seen her alive since June

ep01.h.d_where_w1.l02: Visiting whom? Found even one relative in the south?
ep01.h.version.l01: It adds up. A surname, the weak spot in the deal, the missing owner.
ep01.h.version.l02: It adds up, but it’s flimsy. Half of it you guessed, not found.
ep01.h.version.l03: And you missed more than once. In court there’s no second try.
ep01.h.version.l04: But for now it’s only a theory. To prove it, we have to understand how he finds them.
ep01.h.recon.l02: June. To privatize an apartment, one needs certificates from the housing office, the passport desk, and the BTI. Zoya Pavlovna is in her third week of collecting them.
ep01.h.recon.l03: This is my fourth time here. At one window they say, not us. At another, come back tomorrow.
ep01.h.recon.l04: Forgive me, I couldn’t help overhearing. Not this window, the third. Give me the folder, I’ll look.
ep01.h.recon.l05: Oh, thank you. I don’t understand any of these papers. I want the apartment in my grandson’s name.
ep01.h.recon.l06: I’m a former journalist, used to sorting out papers. I help people free of charge, as a neighbor would. Sergei Viktorovich.
ep01.h.recon.l07: Free? That just doesn’t happen, Sergei Viktorovich.
ep01.h.recon.l08: It does, when you feel sorry for someone.
ep01.h.recon.l09: In a week she will sign the power of attorney without putting on her glasses. At the end of June she will leave home with a bag—and will never return.
ep01.h.d2_late.l01: Tolik, hey, it’s Saiko. Look up a Murashov for me, Sergei Viktorovich: does he have a car? …A Volga? Gray? Read me the plate.
ep01.h.d2_late.l02: A gray Volga under Galina’s windows. Sergei Viktorovich. Murashov. Everything lines up.
ep01.h.d2_late.l03: A gray Volga. Now I need to find who saw it outside Zoya Pavlovna’s building.
ep01.h.d2_late.l04: That’s it, Counselor, I’m going to bed. Run your Murashov yourself tomorrow, I’ve got four MUR cases of my own.
ep01.h.d2_late.l05: Looks like I’ll start tomorrow without him.
ep01.h.d3_office.l02: Palych came in person again. Which means someone called him.
ep01.h.d3_office.l03: Palych walks in without knocking, to check that I’m at my desk.
ep01.h.d3_office.l04: Your case is open. By Friday I expect a man, Gromov, not a piece of paper.
ep01.h.d3_office.l05: It’s Wednesday, Gromov. On Friday, a flawed document on my desk, or a refusal.
ep01.h.d3_office.l06: Kovrigin is complaining to the city: an investigator keeps visiting without a request.
ep01.h.d3_office.l07: And if the notary calls the city again, they’ll take the case. I’m tired of being embarrassed for you.
ep01.h.d3_office.l09: While you were sleeping, Counselor, I wasn’t. Murashov, Sergei Viktorovich, born in 1955, registered in Chertanovo. The gray Volga is his.
ep01.h.d3_office.l10: Saiko’s not here. There’s a note from him on my desk: “At MUR.” I’ll run Murashov myself, through the address bureau. Registered in Chertanovo.
ep01.h.d3_office.l11: This is Irina Lapina. Sergei Viktorovich called last night. Told us to keep quiet, promised to return the money if all stays quiet.
ep01.h.d3_office.l12: He knows we’re looking for him.
ep01.h.d3_office.l13: Gromov, it’s Levina. Grandson’s photo seized, attesting witnesses signed. On the back: “To Grandma from her grandson. Samara.”
ep01.h.d3_office.l14: And her glasses, on the china cabinet, on their case. And the nitroglycerin from the windowsill. All in the report.

ep01.h.d3_route_car.l03: He’s got your face now, Gromov. Did you see him at the window?
ep01.h.d3_route_car.l04: The Lapins already phoned him back. He won’t wait.
ep01.h.d3_route_car.l05: Seen that driver somewhere. I’ll run him tonight.
ep01.h.d3_route_car.l06: The notary’s cracking. A witness, huh… Yeah, right.

ep01.h.d3_route_walk.l03: He watched me leave from the window. He’ll remember.
ep01.h.d3_route_walk.l04: The Lapins have already warned him. He won’t wait.
ep01.h.d3_route_walk.l05: I know where to find him. Now I need something to hold him on.
ep01.h.d3_route_walk.l06: Testimony on the record. I have my document for Friday.

ep01.h.g3c_second.l01: The second card from the file: Khoroshyovka. The owner: an old man living alone, like Zoya Pavlovna. Let’s see who lives there now.
ep01.h.g3w_second.l01: Khoroshyovka, the second card from the file. The owner: an old man living alone, like Zoya Pavlovna. I’ll take the trolleybus and see who lives there now.
ep01.h.g3c_address.l01: Chertanovo, the registered address. Saiko says people like Murashov don’t live where they’re registered. We’ll check.
ep01.h.g3w_address.l01: Chertanovo, the registered address. An hour by metro. People like Murashov don’t usually live where they’re registered.
ep01.h.g3c_kovrigin.l01: Kovrigin. He notarized everything Murashov signed. Let’s see how long he holds out once he realizes this isn’t just one deal.
ep01.h.g3c_kovrigin.l02: Kovrigin. He notarized Zoya Pavlovna’s power of attorney. Let’s see how long he holds out if I ask him point-blank.

ep01.h.second.l02: Saiko stayed downstairs, in the car.
ep01.h.second.l03: Pyotr Ilyich’s door is new, steel—like Zoya Pavlovna’s. I ring the neighbor’s bell.
ep01.h.second.l04: You here for Pyotr Ilyich? Not in. Went to his sister’s in Krasnodar in July—so those new ones say.
ep01.h.second.l06: His sister died ten years ago. He told me so himself—came to my place for tea, Tuesdays.
ep01.h.second.l07: A machinist. His whole life at the lathe. Fixed my iron, my lock. Never took a ruble.
ep01.h.second.l08: And I saw him leave. Morning, in July. He got into a gray Volga. Next to him, this polite one, in a tie. And behind the wheel, another—big, close-cropped, neck like a bull.
ep01.h.second.l09: He didn’t even wave to me. And he always waved.
ep01.h.second.c_klava.statement: Write a statement of all you saw. They’ll look for him
ep01.h.second_statement.l01: A statement… And if that big one comes back?
ep01.h.second_statement.l02: It goes into the case file, not out to the bench by the entrance. They’ll be after him, not you.
ep01.h.second_statement.l03: Give me paper. Pyotr Ilyich would’ve written for me.
ep01.h.second_statement.l04: A statement from a witness: two men took Pyotr Ilyich away in a gray Volga. That’s no longer a search—it’s grounds to open a case.
ep01.h.second_talk.l01: That’s fine. I feel calmer with no papers.
ep01.h.second_talk.l02: She feels calmer. I don’t: a story can’t go into a case file.
ep01.h.address.cap01: Chertanovo. Apartment where Murashov is registered
ep01.h.address.l02: Saiko waits downstairs, in the car.
ep01.h.address.l03: Tenants open the door—the apartment is rented. The landlady lives a floor below and comes up when I ring.
ep01.h.address.l04: Sergei Viktorovich? Pays for the registration neatly, six months ahead. Only he doesn’t live here—has a house out of town. Works in Presnya, at an agency. Where the newspaper used to be.
ep01.h.address.l05: Polite. Brought me flowers on Women’s Day. What did he do?
ep01.h.address.l06: Thank you. We’ll sort it out.
ep01.h.address_office.l02: The sign is new, but the door glass still shows the old word: “Editorial Office.” A gray Volga at the entrance. Someone smokes beside it, back to me.
ep01.h.address_office.c_address.buyer: Go in posing as a buyer
ep01.h.address_office.c_address.watch: Sit in the car and watch
ep01.h.address_office.c_address.leave: Leave. Come back with an arrest warrant
ep01.h.address_buyer.l01: The smoker by the Volga turned around as I walked past. Big, close-cropped.
ep01.h.address_buyer.l02: Inside, the former editorial office. Three phones, files, a carafe. He’s at the desk.
ep01.h.address_buyer.l03: Good afternoon. Are you here about the ad? We have one-room apartments. Our papers are clean. I see to that myself.
ep01.h.address_buyer.l04: Something for my mother. Near the metro.
ep01.h.address_buyer.l05: For your mother—I see. Leave a number and I will call back.
ep01.h.address_buyer.l06: Polite. Colorless. In a line, I wouldn’t have looked at him twice. Only he looked at me a second longer than he needed to.
ep01.h.address_watch.l01: Saiko parks across the road. For three hours we watch the door of the former editorial office.
ep01.h.address_watch.l02: The driver won’t leave the car. Smokes, waits. Has to be the boss’s driver.
ep01.h.address_watch.l03: At six Murashov comes out on the steps, says something to the driver, and goes back in. The driver is big, close-cropped, neck like a bull.
ep01.h.address_watch.l04: The plate matches. I bummed a light off the driver—says they’re in there till midnight, then out of town. So we can pick them up one at a time.
ep01.h.address_leave.l01: I can’t stake it out alone. If I go in, he’ll remember my face. I’m leaving—back with a warrant and a squad.
ep01.h.address_leave.l02: The smoker never turned around. I never saw his face.
ep01.h.kovrigin.l02: A sign on the door: “Notary Anatoly Nikolaevich Kovrigin. Temporarily closed to visitors.” People sit in the hall anyway—out of habit.
ep01.h.kovrigin.l03: Typewriter by the window, abandoned—a sheet still in it.
ep01.h.kovrigin.l04: No Lyuda. Looks like Kovrigin knows who gave him up.
ep01.h.kovrigin.l05: You again. I’ve told you everything.
ep01.h.kovrigin.l06: Prosecutors? I was waiting. Or rather, waiting for someone to come.
ep01.h.kovrigin.l07: Six deals in one summer, Anatoly Nikolaevich. One man with the power of attorney—Murashov. One notary—you.
ep01.h.kovrigin.l08: Three deals in one summer—and that’s not all. One man with the power of attorney—Murashov. One notary—you.
ep01.h.kovrigin.l09: Zoya Pavlovna’s power of attorney, Anatoly Nikolaevich. The man it names—Murashov. Notarized by you.
ep01.h.kovrigin.l10: I notarized it. That’s my job. What people do with their apartments afterward…
ep01.h.kovrigin.l11: Tell me straight: what will happen to me?
ep01.h.kovrigin.c_kovrigin.deal: Testify, and you’ll go as a witness
ep01.h.kovrigin.c_kovrigin.press: You’re an accomplice. Write a confession
ep01.h.kovrigin_deal.l01: A witness… All right. Write it down.
ep01.h.kovrigin_deal.l02: His driver is Dmitry Shmelyov. They call him Shmel. Did time. Drives Sergei Viktorovich around in the Volga and waits outside my windows.
ep01.h.kovrigin_deal.l03: He read the powers of attorney to them himself, out loud. I just asked, “Do you agree?” They nodded.
ep01.h.kovrigin_deal.l04: Dates of the other deals are in the register—I’ll show you. Sergei Viktorovich has an office in Presnya, at the agency where the editorial office used to be. Two blocks away.
ep01.h.kovrigin_deal.l05: He won’t go as a witness. What he is will be decided by the court. He doesn’t know that yet. I do.
ep01.h.kovrigin_press.l01: A confession? Me? Do you know how long I’ve been a notary?
ep01.h.kovrigin_press.l02: Ask Murashov. He’s set up in Presnya, in the agency where the editorial office used to be. And without a lawyer I won’t say another word.
ep01.h.kovrigin_press.l03: He picks up the phone to call his lawyer. The complaint will be on Palych’s desk before I’m back at the office.
ep01.h.d3_evening.l02: Brought the contract? Lamp first—next to the power of attorney.

ep01.h.d3_board.l06: Pin up all you’ve run down. Only what you have—no “probably.”
ep01.h.d3_board.l07: And don’t rush. Tuesday, you guessed half of it.
ep01.h.d3_board_done.l01: It adds up. Every thread leads to one man.
ep01.h.d3_board_done.l02: Not many threads, Gromov. But even these lead to one man.
ep01.h.d3_where.d3_where.relatives: They went to relatives, as everyone was told
ep01.h.d3_where.d3_where.country: They live at his place outside the city
ep01.h.d3_where_w1.l01: Six—and not one called? Not a grandson, not a neighbor?
ep01.h.d3_where_w1.l02: Three—and not one called? Not a grandson, not a neighbor?
ep01.h.d3_where_w1.l03: Zoya Pavlovna went off to relatives—and never once called her grandson?
ep01.h.d3_where_w1.l04: Zoya Pavlovna went off to relatives—and never once called her neighbor?
ep01.h.d3_where_w1.l05: And Pyotr Ilyich—to a sister who’s been dead ten years.
ep01.h.d3_where_w2.l01: Keep them at his place? Apartments sold, money in hand. What does he need them for, Gromov?
ep01.h.d3_night.l01: Three days chasing a signature. Should’ve been chasing people.
ep01.h.d3_night.l02: Go home, Gromov. You’ll need your head tomorrow. And Palych.
ep01.h.d3_night.l03: Gromov, it’s Saiko. I ran your Shmelyov: twenty-seven years old, did time twice. Rough one.
ep01.h.d3_night.l04: Gromov, it’s Saiko. Your driver is Dmitry Shmelyov—Shmel. Twenty-seven, did time twice. Drives Murashov.
ep01.h.d3_night.l05: Yes, Mom. It’s late. No, don’t wait up.
ep01.h.d4_office.l02: This is Irina Lapina. Sergei Viktorovich called in the night—he asked who had come to see us and what we told them.
ep01.h.d4_office.l03: He knows we’re looking for him.
ep01.h.d4_office.l04: Valentin Pavlovich, I need an arrest warrant. Today.
ep01.h.d4_office.l06: Sergei Viktorovich Murashov. The middleman. Six apartments in one summer—and nobody has seen a single owner since.
ep01.h.d4_office.l07: Sergei Viktorovich Murashov. The middleman. Three apartments in one summer—and nobody has seen a single owner since.
ep01.h.d4_office.l08: Sergei Viktorovich Murashov. The middleman. Sold Zoya Pavlovna’s apartment—and nobody has seen her since.
ep01.h.d4_sanction.l01: The case is open, you’ve got a flawed paper. All right.
ep01.h.d4_sanction.l02: Another statement, and your middleman again… It’s not about papers anymore, Gromov. It’s people.
ep01.h.d4_sanction.l03: The notary’s testifying on his own? You’re something, Gromov.
ep01.h.d4_sanction.l04: I’ll sign. But if you take the wrong man, you answer for it yourself.
ep01.h.d4_sanction.l05: Murashov’s photo is from the passport desk, from a card ten years old. I need someone who will recognize him.
ep01.h.d4_sanction.l06: Galina saw him three weeks in a row. But I promised her that her name wouldn’t come up anywhere.
ep01.h.d4_sanction.c_ident.ask: Galina Vasilyevna, only you saw him
ep01.h.d4_sanction.c_ident.spare: Leave her out of it. I promised
ep01.h.d4_sanction.l07: No one to identify him. We take him and sort it out.
ep01.h.d4_ident_irina.l02: Irina looks at the photo for a long time, as if counting to ten.
ep01.h.d4_ident_irina.l03: That’s him. Sergei Viktorovich. He counted the money in the hall at the notary’s—twice, so we’d see.
ep01.h.d4_ident_irina.l04: Write. I’ll sign. No more keeping quiet.
ep01.h.d4_ident_galina.l01: Galina opens at once, no chain. She sees the photo in my hand and understands everything.
ep01.h.d4_ident_galina.l03: I did. But only you saw him.
ep01.h.d4_ident_galina.l04: …That’s him. Sergei Viktorovich. Parked the Volga under my windows.
ep01.h.d4_ident_galina.l05: I’ll sign. But don’t come to see me again.
ep01.h.d4_refuse.l01: On what grounds? Papers are clean, there’s no case. You have missing-person statements—no crime in them. No case, no arrests.
ep01.h.d4_refuse.l03: Then he’ll leave. Hand the inquiry over to the city—let it be their headache.
ep01.h.d4_refuse.l04: Signature, stamp, courier. By evening the inquiry goes to the city.
ep01.h.d4_op.l03: I never asked Galina. I promised, and that’s that.
ep01.h.d4_op.l04: One window is lit in the old editorial office. A gray Volga at the door.
ep01.h.d4_op_choice.l01: Right on schedule. At midnight he comes out, Shmel drives him out of town and comes back alone. We can take them separately.
ep01.h.d4_op_choice.l02: Or now. Both here, both out in the open. Only Shmel’s right pocket is sagging.
ep01.h.d4_op_now.l01: The Volga’s trunk is open. He’s leaving—we can’t wait.
ep01.h.d4_op_now.l02: No Saiko. I have two sergeants from the precinct. We take them at once.
ep01.h.d4_op_now.l03: No Saiko. Two sergeants from the precinct are with me.
ep01.h.d4_op_now.l04: We have no schedule. Waiting means guessing. We take them now.
ep01.h.d4_op_now.l06: Saiko is sitting on the asphalt, holding his shoulder.
ep01.h.d4_op_now.l07: Just a scratch, Counselor. Go get your man. The guys have the driver.
ep01.h.d4_op_now.l08: License says the driver is Dmitry Shmelyov. Has a record, the sergeant says.
ep01.h.d4_op_now.l09: The driver escapes through the courtyards. The sergeant runs after him, returns alone.
ep01.h.d4_op_now.l10: We take Murashov on the stairs. He doesn’t run, doesn’t ask anything. He holds out his hands—like someone in line for a certificate.
ep01.h.d4_op_wait.l01: Midnight. Murashov comes out, Shmelyov opens the door for him. The Volga heads out of town—a precinct car follows it with its headlights off.
ep01.h.d4_op_wait.l02: At half past one it returns—alone. Shmelyov is taken at the metro: there’s no time to pull his hand from his pocket.
ep01.h.d4_op_wait.l05: And says nothing till the precinct.
ep01.h.d4_search.l01: Murashov was picked up at dawn, on the porch of his house out of town. He didn’t run. He didn’t ask anything.
ep01.h.d4_search.l03: Files by year, a carafe, a ficus on the windowsill. The office of a man whose affairs are in order.
ep01.h.d4_search.l04: Gromov, where do we start? The lawyer’s coming soon—we can’t turn the place upside down.
ep01.h.d4_search.l05: The lawyer arrives soon. I won’t get through everything.
ep01.h.d4_search.c_search.papers: Folders. Powers of attorney, receipts, contracts
ep01.h.d4_search.c_search.keys: Keys and belongings. Anything that isn’t his
ep01.h.d4_search_papers.l01: Powers of attorney. Six of them, all in his name, all notarized by Kovrigin.
ep01.h.d4_search_papers.l02: I knew that already—from the card file.
ep01.h.d4_search_papers.l03: In the card file I found fewer. Now there are six—all on paper.
ep01.h.d4_search_papers.l04: Six. And I knew about one—Zoya Pavlovna’s.
ep01.h.d4_search_papers.l05: I never got to the desk drawers: the lawyer arrived.
ep01.h.d4_search_keys.l01: In the bottom drawer, a bunch of keys. Each has a cardboard tag, an address in his handwriting.
ep01.h.d4_search_keys.l02: Under the keys, passports. Other people’s. On top is Zoya Pavlovna’s.
ep01.h.d4_search_keys.l03: A woman’s bag is there too. Galina said Zoya Pavlovna left the house with it at the end of June.
ep01.h.d4_search_keys.l04: A woman’s old cloth bag is there too.
ep01.h.d5_field.l02: Shmelyov showed the place at night. Asked for the map himself.
ep01.h.d5_field.l03: Shmelyov talked at night: “I just drove.” He asked for the map himself and showed the place.
ep01.h.d5_field.l04: Tape strung between the birches. Shovels. Levina in rubber boots walks along the tape and says nothing.
ep01.h.d5_field.l05: I stand by the car. No one calls me closer—and I don’t ask.
ep01.h.d5_field.l06: Six, Gromov. As many as there were deals.
ep01.h.d5_field.l08: Saiko is at Botkin Hospital. He called at six, asked, “Found them?” and hung up.
ep01.h.d5_field.l09: Saiko smokes by the car. Doesn’t joke.
ep01.h.d5_interrog.l02: He sits down, adjusts his cuffs, and waits for me to begin.
ep01.h.d5_interrog.l03: I like it when people work by the book. Please, ask. All my papers are in order.
ep01.h.d5_interrog.l04: His papers are in order. And the people?
ep01.h.d5_after.l01: Write it down. I’ll dictate by date. Word for word.
ep01.h.d5_after.l02: He dictates evenly, like filling out a form: dates, addresses, amounts. Not one extra word.
ep01.h.d5_after.l03: The deals—yes. Powers of attorney—yes. The rest you must prove.
ep01.h.d5_after.l05: To the end of the interrogation he watches not me but my hand writing the official record.
ep01.h.d5_confront.l01: Confrontation. Kovrigin is seated opposite. He stares at the table.
ep01.h.d5_confront.l02: Anatoly Nikolaevich, you remember everything. It was all done lawfully.
ep01.h.d5_confront.c_confront.press: You knew, Anatoly Nikolaevich. You knew all summer
ep01.h.d5_confront.c_confront.calm: Repeat what you wrote. Calmly, in order
ep01.h.d5_confront_press.l01: Knew?… You promised I’d be a witness. And now it’s “knew”?
ep01.h.d5_confront_press.l02: I withdraw my testimony. Not a word without a lawyer.
ep01.h.d5_confront_press.l03: He really won’t be a witness. But now I don’t have his testimony either.
ep01.h.d5_confront_calm.l01: He read it to them. Himself, out loud. I only asked, “Do you agree?” They nodded.
ep01.h.d5_confront_calm.l02: I also charged for rushing it. Write that down.
ep01.h.d5_confront_calm.l03: Anatoly Nikolaevich is tired. He should get some rest.
ep01.h.d5_confront_calm.l04: His first line today that isn’t about papers.
ep01.h.d5_boss.l02: See it through, Gromov. You’ve earned it.
ep01.h.d5_boss.l03: The city’s taking the case. No offense: they have people and deadlines, you have papers and nerves.
ep01.h.d5_boss.l05: Gromov? Calling from Botkin. Arm’s still on—doctor says I got lucky.
ep01.h.d5_boss.l06: On the line I can hear his wife say to him, “Give it here. Enough already.”
ep01.h.d5_gone.l03: The agency is closed. A sign on the door: “Closed for repairs.” No Volga out front.
ep01.h.d5_gone.l04: Gone, Gromov. Overnight, with his stuff. Neighbors saw.
ep01.h.d5_gone.l05: The neighbors saw it: things loaded into a gray Volga at night.
ep01.h.d5_gone.l06: The file’s at the city prosecutor’s office. My signature’s on the last page.
ep01.h.fin_zoya.l02: For forty years she was a proofreader at a printing house on Presnya. She spotted typos in other people’s texts at first glance.
ep01.h.fin_zoya.l03: She raised her grandson on her own. When he left to study in Samara, she wrote to him every Sunday.
ep01.h.fin_zoya.l04: She had meant to leave the apartment on Molodogvardeyskaya Street to him.
ep01.h.fin_zoya.l05: Pyotr Ilyich R. 1914–1993. A machinist, at the lathe all his life. He fixed the neighbors’ irons and locks, and never took money for it.
ep01.h.fin_court.l03: The Moscow City Court found Murashov guilty of murders committed for financial gain and sentenced him to the exceptional measure of punishment—the death penalty.
ep01.h.fin_court.l05: The verdict covered only the counts that the investigation had managed to prove.
ep01.h.fin_court.cap06: A moratorium on the death penalty has been in effect in Russia since 1996.
ep01.h.fin_court.l07: Murashov’s sentence was never carried out: the exceptional measure was replaced with life imprisonment.
ep01.h.fin_court.l08: Shmelyov was detained a day later, at Kazansky Station.
ep01.h.fin_court.l09: Kovrigin, the notary, was sentenced to six years and lost the right to notarize documents. Shmelyov was sentenced to twelve.
ep01.h.fin_court.l10: At the trial Kovrigin repeated only one thing: “They promised me.”
ep01.h.fin_court.l11: Murashov did not say a word at the trial. He only asked that the record be kept verbatim.
ep01.h.fin_epilogue.l02: By court order, the apartment on Molodogvardeyskaya Street was returned to the grandson from Samara.
ep01.h.fin_epilogue.l03: The photograph from the china cabinet was given to him along with the keys.
ep01.h.fin_epilogue.l04: The Lapins gave testimony, and by court order part of their money was returned.
ep01.h.fin_epilogue.l05: The Lapins learned everything from a summons.
ep01.h.fin_epilogue.l06: Galina identified Murashov—and a year later moved to her daughter’s in Tula. She left Gromov no address.
ep01.h.fin_epilogue.l07: Galina’s name was never mentioned in the case.
ep01.h.fin_epilogue.l08: Galina left for Tula as early as August and never came back to Moscow.
ep01.h.fin_epilogue.l09: Galina never learned that her statement had become a case.
ep01.h.fin_epilogue.l10: Lyuda left the notary’s office and began studying law.
ep01.h.fin_epilogue.l11: Kovrigin’s assistant did not return to the office from her leave.
ep01.h.fin_epilogue.l12: Klavdia Semyonovna attended every session of the trial.
ep01.h.fin_epilogue.l13: Shmelyov pointed out the site near Aprelevka only in the spring of 1994.
ep01.h.fin_epilogue.l14: Saiko returned after four months. His right arm never rose above the shoulder again.
ep01.h.fin_epilogue.l15: Saiko received a commendation in an official order.
ep01.h.fin_epilogue.l16: Saiko returned to his own cases at MUR. When Murashov was detained in Tver, he was the first to call Gromov.
ep01.h.fin_epilogue.l17: Saiko learned how the case ended from an internal summary.
ep01.h.fin_epilogue.l18: Valentin Pavlovich retired in 1995. At his send-off he said of Gromov: “Inconvenient. But he saw it through.”
ep01.h.fin_epilogue.l19: Valentin Pavlovich retired in 1995. The Murashov case was not mentioned at his send-off.
ep01.h.fin_epilogue.l20: Murashov was detained in Tver in the spring of 1994—by others. Gromov was transferred to economic cases.
ep01.h.fin_epilogue.l21: The city prosecutor’s office took the case to its conclusion. Gromov was transferred to economic cases.
ep01.h.fin_epilogue.l22: Gromov stayed in Kuntsevo. Apartment cases now came to him first.
ep01.h.fin_journal.l01: Galina was promised that her name would not be mentioned—and was asked to make an identification.
ep01.h.fin_journal.l02: Galina was promised that her name would not be mentioned—and the promise was kept.
ep01.h.fin_journal.l03: Galina was told, “It’s your duty”—and she left.
ep01.h.fin_journal.l04: Galina was spoken to formally, for the record—and the chain on her door never came off.
ep01.h.fin_journal.l05: No one ever went to see Galina.
ep01.h.fin_journal.l06: Kovrigin was promised he would be a witness. The court decided otherwise.
ep01.h.fin_journal.l07: Kovrigin was promised nothing—and said only where to look for Murashov.
ep01.h.fin_journal.l08: No one went to see Kovrigin on Wednesday.
ep01.h.fin_journal.l09: The arrest warrant was denied—and that same night Murashov left.
ep01.h.fin_journal.l10: They waited at the agency until midnight—and detained both men separately.
ep01.h.fin_journal.l11: The arrest was made at once—and the bullet hit Saiko.
ep01.h.fin_journal.l12: The arrest was made at once, without Saiko—and Shmelyov escaped through the courtyards.
ep01.h.fin_journal.l13: The arrest was made at once, without Saiko—and the driver escaped through the courtyards.
ep01.h.fin_2004.l02: The grandchildren still write to me. Not about Murashov—about the old people. They ask what they were like. All I know is what their papers were like.
ep01.mg_docs.title: Document Check
ep01.mg_docs.brief: Compare the power of attorney and the contract. Mark the place where they do not match.
ep01.mg_docs.hint.date: The certification date has been written over another digit
ep01.mg_docs.f.contract_poa_ref: under power of attorney dated June 11, 1993
ep01.mg_docs.f.contract_notary: Certified by notary A. N. Kovrigin
ep01.mg_db.title: BTI Card Index
ep01.mg_db.brief: Select the cards with the same notary and the same attorney-in-fact as in Zoya Pavlovna’s deal.
ep01.mg_docs.hint.ref: The contract cites one date for the power of attorney; the power of attorney itself shows another
ep01.h.mg_board.title: Levina’s Board
ep01.h.mg_board.brief: Connect the people, apartments, and items. The board shows only what you have found.
ep01.h.mg_interrogation_hod.title: Murashov’s Interrogation
ep01.h.mg_interrogation_hod.brief: Present evidence against the statement. Evidence you did not find is unavailable. Three mistakes and he stops talking.
ep01.h.mg_interrogation_hod.st.south: Zoya Pavlovna went south to stay with relatives. She told me so herself.
ep01.h.mg_interrogation_hod.press.south: She did not say where exactly. I have no right to ask an adult for her address.
ep01.h.mg_interrogation_hod.st.read: She read the power of attorney herself and signed before the notary.
ep01.h.mg_interrogation_hod.press.read: The notary certified her signature. That is his job, not mine. Ask him.
ep01.h.mg_interrogation_hod.st.free: I helped old people with their paperwork for free. As a neighbor.
ep01.h.mg_interrogation_hod.press.free: Certificates, taxis, lines—I covered the expenses myself. That is not prohibited.
ep01.h.mg_interrogation_hod.st.shmel: I do not know that driver. Anyone might be standing outside a building.
ep01.h.mg_interrogation_hod.press.shmel: I hire drivers from advertisements. I do not ask their surnames. I pay for the trip.
ep01.h.mg_interrogation_hod.st.where: I do not know where they are. They are adults; they went where they wished.
ep01.h.mg_interrogation_hod.press.where: I am not their guardian. I received the money and passed it on. My receipts are in order.
ep01.h.mg_interrogation_hod.ev.photo: Photo of the grandson in Samara
ep01.h.mg_interrogation_hod.ev.read: Kovrigin: Murashov read her the power of attorney
ep01.h.mg_flat_inspect.title: What Did She Leave When “Heading South”?
ep01.h.mg_flat_inspect.brief: The Lapins are watching. You cannot search for long.
ep01.h.mg_flat_inspect.hs.photo: Grandson’s photo in the china cabinet
ep01.h.mg_flat_inspect.why.photo: Zoya Pavlovna has one relative: a grandson in Samara. Yet the Lapins were told she went south to relatives. Gromov will ask them about it right away.
ep01.h.mg_flat_inspect.clue.glasses: What she could not read without
ep01.h.mg_flat_inspect.why.glasses: Zoya Pavlovna cannot read without glasses, so she signed the power of attorney without reading it. Who read it to her?
ep01.h.mg_flat_inspect.clue.pills: What she never left home without
ep01.h.mg_flat_inspect.why.pills: Nitroglycerin. A heart patient does not leave home without it, so she did not go south.
ep01.h.mg_flat_inspect.why.calendar: No pages torn off since June 27. On June 28 the Lapins were already buying the apartment: the owner “left” a day before the sale.
ep01.h.mg_flat_inspect.clue.pension: What she needs to get her pension
ep01.h.mg_flat_inspect.why.pension: Without the ID, the post office will not pay her pension. No one leaving for the summer leaves it behind—she was only stepping out.
ep01.h.note.n_statement.title: Galina’s Statement
ep01.h.note.n_south.title: Lapins: “She Went South”
ep01.h.note.n_south.text: The apartment was bought on June 28 from an attorney-in-fact. The Lapins were told the owner had gone to relatives in the south. The china cabinet with its dishes was hers; it stayed in the apartment.
ep01.h.note.n_contract.title: Sale Contract
ep01.h.note.n_poa.title: Power of Attorney (Copy)
ep01.h.note.n_poa.text: POWER OF ATTORNEY. City of Moscow, June 14, 1993. I, Zoya Pavlovna S., residing at Molodogvardeyskaya St., apt. 34, hereby authorize Sergei Viktorovich Murashov to sell the apartment belonging to me at a price and on terms at his own discretion and to receive the money due to me. Certified by notary A. N. Kovrigin, entered in the register.
ep01.h.note.n_name.title: Attorney-in-Fact: Murashov, S. V.
ep01.h.note.n_name.text: Zoya Pavlovna’s apartment was sold under the power of attorney by Sergei Viktorovich Murashov.
ep01.h.note.n_cash.title: Cash Paid at the Notary’s
ep01.h.note.n_cash.text: The middleman rushed the Lapins: payment in cash, right in Kovrigin’s office, in the hallway.
ep01.h.note.n_photo.title: Grandson’s Photo
ep01.h.note.n_photo.text: Behind the glass of the china cabinet. On the back, in pencil: “To Grandma from her grandson. Samara.” She has only one relative: a grandson in Samara.
ep01.h.note.n_left.title: Galina: Left in Late June
ep01.h.note.n_left.text: In late June Zoya Pavlovna walked out of the building with a bag. Galina never saw her again.
ep01.h.note.n_sergei.title: Galina: “Sergei Viktorovich”
ep01.h.note.n_sergei.text: Polite, “from a newspaper.” For three weeks he helped Zoya Pavlovna with her papers. Came in a gray Volga and parked under Galina’s windows, not at the entrance.
ep01.h.note.n_last_seen.title: Galina: Last Seen
ep01.h.note.n_last_seen.text: In late June Zoya Pavlovna left with a bag, in her good raincoat. She said Sergei Viktorovich would stop by, about the papers. She has not been seen since.
ep01.h.note.n_register.title: Kovrigin’s Register
ep01.h.note.n_register.text: The entry for the June 14 power of attorney is in different ink, bluer than the lines around it. Kovrigin: “a technical error by my assistant.”
ep01.h.note.n_lyuda.title: Notary’s Assistant
ep01.h.note.n_lyuda.text: Lyuda: Sergei Viktorovich comes often, always with old people, and skips the line. For rush service he pays Kovrigin in cash, into his desk.
ep01.h.note.n_vypiska.title: Housing Office: Deregistered June 25
ep01.h.note.n_vypiska.text: Zoya Pavlovna was deregistered from the apartment on June 25, on the application of the attorney-in-fact. She did not come in herself. He brought the passport clerk a chocolate bar.
ep01.h.note.n_queue.title: Housing Office: In the Line All Summer
ep01.h.note.n_queue.text: All summer a polite man hung around the line at the housing office, talking to the old women and filling out forms for them.
ep01.h.note.n_card.title: BTI Record Card
ep01.h.note.n_card.text: Molodogvardeyskaya St., apt. 34. Transfer of title: contract dated June 28, 1993, notary A. N. Kovrigin. Seller’s representative by power of attorney: S. V. Murashov.
ep01.h.note.n_bti3.title: Three Deals in One Summer—and More
ep01.h.note.n_bti3.text: At least three apartments of elderly people living alone: notary Kovrigin, attorney-in-fact S. V. Murashov. Gromov was not allowed to finish going through the card file.
ep01.h.note.n_bti.title: Six Deals in One Summer
ep01.h.note.n_bti.text: Six apartments of elderly people living alone. The notary is Kovrigin in every one; the attorney-in-fact is S. V. Murashov in every one.
ep01.h.note.n_date.title: Date on the Power of Attorney
ep01.h.note.n_date.text: The contract refers to a power of attorney dated June 11, while the power of attorney itself says the 14th. Levina: the 4 is written over a 1, and there is no “correction certified” note. A flawed document.
ep01.h.note.n_glasses.title: Zoya Pavlovna’s Glasses
ep01.h.note.n_glasses.text: Left at home, on top of the china cabinet, on the glasses case. She cannot read without glasses: she signed the power of attorney without reading it.
ep01.h.note.n_pills.title: Pills on the Windowsill
ep01.h.note.n_pills.text: Nitroglycerin. A heart patient does not leave home without it. She did not go south.
ep01.h.note.n_calendar.title: Calendar on June 27
ep01.h.note.n_calendar.text: A tear-off calendar by the kitchen: no pages torn off since June 27. On June 28 the Lapins were already buying the apartment.
ep01.h.note.n_pension.title: Pension ID
ep01.h.note.n_pension.text: Left at home, on the bed. Without it the pension will not be paid out: she was only stepping out for a short while.
ep01.h.note.n_read.title: Murashov Read Her the Power of Attorney
ep01.h.note.n_read.text: Kovrigin: the old lady had no glasses, so the attorney-in-fact read her the text—Murashov himself. “The law allows it.”
ep01.h.note.n_call.title: The Lapins Called the Notary
ep01.h.note.n_call.text: The middleman told the Lapins to call the notary if anyone came from the police. The notary and the middleman are working together.
ep01.h.note.n_address.title: Murashov’s Registered Address
ep01.h.note.n_address.text: Murashov, Sergei Viktorovich, born 1955. Registered in Chertanovo.
ep01.h.note.n_volga.title: Murashov’s Volga
ep01.h.note.n_volga.text: The gray Volga is registered to S. V. Murashov. Saiko ran the plate.
ep01.h.note.n_irina.title: Irina: Sergei Viktorovich Called
ep01.h.note.n_irina.text: Murashov called the Lapins: told them to keep quiet and promised to return their money if everything stayed quiet. He knows he is being looked for.
ep01.h.note.n_pyotr.title: Pyotr Ilyich, Age 79
ep01.h.note.n_pyotr.text: Khoroshyovka, the second apartment in the card file. Retired machinist. “Went to his sister’s in Krasnodar” in July—but his sister died ten years ago.
ep01.h.note.n_driver.title: Klavdia Semyonovna: The Driver
ep01.h.note.n_driver.text: Pyotr Ilyich was taken away in July in a gray Volga. Next to him sat a polite man in a tie; at the wheel, a big man with a buzz cut.
ep01.h.note.n_klava.title: A Witness Statement
ep01.h.note.n_klava.text: Klavdia Semyonovna wrote a statement: two men took Pyotr Ilyich away in a gray Volga. This is no longer a missing-person search but grounds for a case.
ep01.h.note.n_office.title: Agency on Presnya
ep01.h.note.n_office.text: Murashov works at a real estate agency on Presnya, in a former newspaper office.
ep01.h.note.n_seen.title: Murashov Seen in Person
ep01.h.note.n_seen.text: Gromov went into the agency posing as a buyer. Murashov, polite and colorless, remembered his face.
ep01.h.note.n_watch.title: Murashov’s Schedule
ep01.h.note.n_watch.text: Murashov stays at the agency until midnight; then the driver takes him out of town and comes back alone. They can be taken separately.
ep01.h.note.n_kovrigin.title: Kovrigin’s Testimony
ep01.h.note.n_kovrigin.text: On the record: Murashov read the powers of attorney aloud to the old people; the dates of the other deals are in the register. Kovrigin has been promised he will be a witness.
ep01.h.note.n_shmel.title: Dmitry Shmelyov (“Shmel”)
ep01.h.note.n_sanction.title: Arrest Warrant
ep01.h.note.n_sanction.text: Palych signed the arrest warrant for Murashov.
ep01.h.note.n_ident.title: Identification
ep01.h.note.n_ident.text: Murashov was identified from the photo from the passport desk.
ep01.h.note.n_shmel_talks.title: Shmelyov: “Drove Them to the Woods”
ep01.h.note.n_shmel_talks.text: “I just drove. Drove them to the woods.” He pointed out the place himself.
ep01.h.note.n_keys.title: Tagged Keys
ep01.h.note.n_keys.text: From the search: keys to other people’s apartments with tags, addresses in his handwriting; the old people’s passports; Zoya Pavlovna’s bag.
ep01.h.note.n_field.title: Woodland Strip near Aprelevka
ep01.title: Death for Apartments
ep01.logline: August 1993. Pensioners are vanishing, and their apartments are sold with spotless paperwork. Investigator Gromov runs the case himself: where to go, whom to question, what to believe.
